title: China: the yuan in US cents, monthly averages of daily rates, January 1929 - December 1936 (Banking and Monetary Statistics, Table 173)
source: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Banking and Monetary Statistics 1914-1941 (Washington, 1943), Table 173, 'Foreign exchange rates, by countries, monthly', China (p. 667): averages of daily rates, cents per unit of Chinese currency; FRASER, https://fraser.stlouisfed.org/files/docs/publications/bms/1914-1941/BMS14-41_complete.pdf (SHA-256 ca7b8e3161d21ecf3bd804accd901eb3234397146f5cd091d6388e1027d2387e), PDF page 665
series: year; month; cents_per_yuan: US cents per yuan, the monthly average of daily rates
license: Public domain (a publication of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, 1943).
notes: Read from the text layer (pdftotext -layout) and checked on images of the page rendered with pdftoppm at 200 dpi. The text layer misreads April 1933 ('322. 1953': footnote 3 and 22.1953), the year 1933 ('328.5979': footnote 3 and 28.5979) and July 1935 ('3'8.6791'). Footnote 3: 'Average of quotations for new yuan beginning April 10' (1933; the standard yuan of March 1933). The table also gives the tael and the Mexican dollar to 1932; the yuan column is used throughout. From April 1933 the dollar was off gold (Chapter 28) and from 31 January 1934 it was fixed at $35 an ounce, so a cent after March 1933 is no longer the cent of the gold dollar of $20.67 an ounce.
citation: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (1943), Banking and Monetary Statistics 1914-1941, Table 173
